message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"9.11","text":"And in prayers one must also confess that one has taken refuge in God and solemnly affirm that, on the demon’s part, it is not disobedience but delay. For everything comes to pass for the one who believes, but nothing for the one who does not believe. Hence the demons themselves, knowing the quantity of faith possessed by those whom they overpower, allot a proportionate measure of their own persistence. For this reason they persist with those who do not believe, linger with those who have difficulty believing, but cannot remain even for an instant with those who have believed completely and act well. For the soul, having been turned by faith toward God as though into the nature of water, extinguishes the demon like a spark of fire. It is therefore difficult for each person to recognize the flight of the demon within them. For by blending themselves with souls, the demons suggest to each person’s mind thoughts directed toward whatever they wish, so that the person neglects their own salvation.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸ θεῷ προσπεφευγέναι","chosen":"that one has taken refuge in God","rationale":"The perfect infinitive presents recourse to God as an accomplished act with a continuing state."},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ἀπείθειαν, ἀλλὰ βραδυτῆτα","chosen":"not disobedience but delay","rationale":"The contrast concerns the demon’s delayed departure rather than outright refusal."},{"source_quote":"τῆς πίστεως τὴν ποσότητα","chosen":"the quantity of faith","rationale":"The wording explicitly presents faith as possessing a measurable degree or amount."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς δὲ δυσπίστοις ἐνβραδύνουσιν","chosen":"linger with those who have difficulty believing","rationale":"δύσπιστος denotes difficulty or reluctance in believing, distinguished here from outright unbelief."},{"source_quote":"κάματος οὖν ἐστὶν","chosen":"It is therefore difficult","rationale":"κάματος literally denotes labor or weariness and here characterizes recognition as laborious or difficult."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.12","text":"Hence many, not knowing where the power acting on them comes from, assent to the evil notions suggested by demons as though they were the reasoning of their own soul. Therefore they become more reluctant to go to those capable of saving them; and while being consumed by the very demons lying in wait for them, they fail to recognize those people. The demons lurking in the innermost recesses of their souls prompt them to suppose that it is not a demon troubling them but a bodily disease—such as acrid matter, bile, phlegm, an imbalance of blood, inflammation of the meninges, or something else—. . . . But even if this were so, not even that is exempt from being a form of demon. For the universal and earthy soul, which extends through all foods as their cause, when taken in to a greater extent through more abundant food, itself unites with the spirit as something kindred to it—the spirit being the soul of a human being—while the material portion of the food, once united with the body, is smeared upon it like a terrible poison. Therefore self-sufficiency is good in everything.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πόθεν ἐνεργοῦνται","chosen":"where the power acting on them comes from","rationale":"The passive verb describes an agency or power operating upon them, while πόθεν asks its source."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τοὺς ὑπ’ αὐτῶν τῶν ἐνεδρευόντων δαιμόνων ἀναλισκόμενοι ἀγνοοῦσιν","chosen":"and while being consumed by the very demons lying in wait for them, they fail to recognize those people","rationale":"The accusative τοὺς is taken anaphorically as the object of ἀγνοοῦσιν, referring to the people capable of saving them; ἀναλισκόμενοι describes those who fail to recognize their prospective helpers."},{"source_quote":"ἐνδομυχούντων δαιμόνων","chosen":"demons lurking in the innermost recesses","rationale":"ἐνδομυχέω depicts dwelling or hiding deep within an interior recess."},{"source_quote":"ὕλης δριμείας","chosen":"acrid matter","rationale":"In the medical list ὕλη denotes bodily matter or material; “acrid humor” is possible but would impose a more specific technical sense."},{"source_quote":"δαίμονος εἶδος εἶναι","chosen":"being a form of demon","rationale":"The phrase categorizes the proposed bodily condition as a manifestation or kind of demon within the author’s framework."},{"source_quote":"ἡ γὰρ καθόλου καὶ γεώδης ψυχή","chosen":"For the universal and earthy soul","rationale":"καθόλου and γεώδης characterize this soul as universal and earth-associated; “general terrestrial soul” is a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἡ αὐτάρκεια","chosen":"self-sufficiency","rationale":"In this dietary context αὐτάρκεια may imply contentment, sufficiency, or moderation, but the main rendering retains its broader sense."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ τοὺς ὑπ’ αὐτῶν τῶν ἐνεδρευόντων δαιμόνων ἀναλισκόμενοι ἀγνοοῦσιν","issue":"The placement of the accusative τοὺς before the intervening participial phrase is marked, but it can defensibly function as an anaphoric object of ἀγνοοῦσιν, referring back to τοὺς σώζειν αὐτοὺς δυναμένους. The main text follows that reading. If τοὺς is not anaphoric, the construction becomes irregular and deletion might be conjectured, but no correction is adopted.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἢ ἄλλου τινός) . . . . εἰ δὲ καὶ τοῦτο ἦν","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna marked by exactly four dots. Its content is unavailable, and no restoration has been supplied; the same four-dot gap remains explicit in the translation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"9.13","text":"Some of the wicked demons lie in wait in another way. At first they do not even reveal that they exist, so that no effort against them may arise; but at an opportune moment, under the pretext of anger, erotic passion, or something else, they suddenly assault the body by a sword, a noose, a precipice, or some other means. And, having entered the purifying fire, as we said, they bring it about that the deceived souls of those who have been mingled with them will be punished to the end. Others, being ambushed in another way, do not approach us, because they are deceived by the thoughts of the wicked demons into supposing that they suffer these things from their own gods because of their neglect toward them, that they can reconcile those gods through sacrifices, and that they must not approach us but, on the contrary, must flee and hate us. And all the same, they hate and flee those who have greater compassion for them and pursue them in order to benefit them.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὴν ἀρχὴν οὐδὲ ὅτι εἰσὶν ἐνφαίνοντες","chosen":"At first they do not even reveal that they exist","rationale":"τὴν ἀρχήν can mean “at the beginning” or idiomatically “at all”; the subsequent reference to an opportune occasion favors a temporal contrast."},{"source_quote":"ὀργῆς προφάσει, ἔρωτος ἢ ἄλλου τινὸς","chosen":"under the pretext of anger, erotic passion, or something else","rationale":"ἔρως here denotes passionate or erotic desire, while πρόφασις presents these emotions as pretexts or occasions."},{"source_quote":"τὸ σῶμα αἰφνιδίως ἐνυβρίζουσιν","chosen":"they suddenly assault the body","rationale":"ἐνυβρίζω conveys violent mistreatment or outrage against the body."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τέλος κολασθησομένας καθιστᾶσιν","chosen":"they bring it about that ... will be punished to the end","rationale":"The future passive participle κολασθησομένας gives the punishment prospective force. εἰς τέλος may mean “to the end,” “completely,” or, in some contexts, “forever”; the source-transparent wording leaves its extent unresolved."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὸ καθάρσιον χωρήσαντες πῦρ","chosen":"having entered the purifying fire","rationale":"χωρήσαντες is nominative masculine plural and most directly resumes the demons as grammatical subject. A contextual association with the people mingled with them is possible despite the case difference."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμῶς","chosen":"And all the same","rationale":"ὁμῶς can mean “alike” or “all the same”; the latter preserves the ironic contrast with the compassion shown to them."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.14","text":"Thus, by hating and fleeing us, they are ensnared, not knowing from what source it comes about that they think things contrary to their own salvation. For neither can we compel them, when they are unwilling, to incline toward salvation—since we do not now have such authority over them—nor can they by themselves recognize the demon’s evil thought, for they do not know from where the thoughts of evil are suggested to them. These are the people whom the demons terrify by appearing in whatever forms they wish. Sometimes they also prescribe treatments for the sick, and in this way they gain among those already deceived a reputation as gods and conceal from most people that they are demons—but not from us, who know their secret, the reason why they do such things, transforming themselves in dreams against those over whom they have authority. Some they terrify; to others they issue oracles, demand sacrifices, and command them to share a feast, so that they may drink down their souls along with them.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς σωτηρίαν νεῦσαι","chosen":"to incline toward salvation","rationale":"νεύω depicts leaning, inclining, or signaling assent rather than merely moving physically."},{"source_quote":"τὴν κακὴν τοῦ δαίμονος ἐνθύμησιν","chosen":"the demon’s evil thought","rationale":"ἐνθύμησις can denote a thought, consideration, or inward suggestion; the genitive identifies the demon as its source."},{"source_quote":"θεραπείας συντάσσουσιν","chosen":"prescribe treatments","rationale":"συντάσσω can mean arrange or prescribe, and θεραπεία here refers to treatment or care for the sick."},{"source_quote":"θεῶν δόξαν ἀποφέρονται","chosen":"they gain ... a reputation as gods","rationale":"δόξα here is reputation or estimation, while θεῶν expresses the status attributed to them."},{"source_quote":"ἑαυτοὺς κατ’ ὄναρ καθ’ ὧν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἔχουσι μεταμορφοῦντες","chosen":"transforming themselves in dreams against those over whom they have authority","rationale":"The first κατά marks the dream setting; the second can bear the adversative sense “against.” It may alternatively refer more generally to those subject to their power."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα αὐτῶν τὰς ψυχὰς συνπίνωσιν","chosen":"so that they may drink down their souls along with them","rationale":"The souls are the accusative object of συνπίνωσιν. The compound evokes drinking together at the feast while portraying the demons as consuming the participants’ souls."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.15","text":"For just as formidable snakes draw sparrows toward themselves with their breaths, so these demons also draw those who partake of their table into their own will, having mixed themselves into their minds through the food and drink. They transform themselves in dreams according to the likenesses of the carved images in order to increase the deception. For the carved image is neither a living creature nor does it possess a divine spirit; rather, the demon that was seen made use of its form. To how many others have they similarly appeared in dreams, and did those people not agree when they met one another while awake and compared what was in the dream? Consequently, what might appear is no longer a dream; rather, it either belongs to a demon or consists of the products of a soul that assigns the forms to fears in the cheek and to desire. For, alternatively, when its mind has been struck by fear, it gives birth to the forms through dreams. But if you think that the carved images, since they are animate, can perform such things, set them on a balance when its beam is level, place the counterweight on the other pan, and call upon them to become either heavier or lighter. If that happens, they are animate; but it does not happen. If, however, it should happen, such a thing is in that way a god. For even this can happen by the finger of a demon. Worms also move, and they are not called gods.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ δεινοὶ ὄφεις τοῖς αὐτῶν πνεύμασιν τοὺς στρουθοὺς ἐπισπῶνται","chosen":"formidable snakes draw sparrows toward themselves with their breaths","rationale":"πνεύματα here are the snakes’ breaths or exhalations, and στρουθοί most naturally denotes sparrows or small birds."},{"source_quote":"διά γε τῶν βρωτῶν καὶ ποτῶν ἀνακραθέντες αὐτῶν τῷ νῷ","chosen":"having mixed themselves into their minds through the food and drink","rationale":"ἀνακραθέντες portrays the demons as becoming mixed with the participants’ mind by means of what is eaten and drunk."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὰς τῶν ξοάνων ἰδέας","chosen":"according to the likenesses of the carved images","rationale":"ξόανον is a carved cult image, often wooden, while ἰδέαι here are its visible forms or likenesses."},{"source_quote":"πόσοις κατ’ ὄναρ ὁμοίως ἄλλοις ὤφθησαν καὶ ὕπαρ συναντήσαντες ἀλλήλοις πρὸς τὸ κατ’ ὄναρ ἀντιβάλλοντες οὐ συνεφώνησαν;","chosen":"To how many others have they similarly appeared in dreams, and did those people not agree when they met one another while awake and compared what was in the dream?","rationale":"The clauses are coordinated by καί, and οὐ συνεφώνησαν is retained as a negative question expecting agreement rather than converted into an assertion that they disagreed."},{"source_quote":"ὕπαρ συναντήσαντες ἀλλήλοις","chosen":"when they met one another while awake","rationale":"ὕπαρ contrasts waking experience with what was experienced in a dream."},{"source_quote":"ὥστε οὐκέτι ὄναρ ἐπιφανείη ἐκεῖνό ἐστιν","chosen":"Consequently, what might appear is no longer a dream","rationale":"The rendering takes ἐκεῖνο as the subject associated with optative ἐπιφανείη and ὄναρ as the predicate of ἐστιν. The construction is irregular, and an alternative sense is that the appearance is no longer merely a dream apparition."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς παρίᾳ φόβοις καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἀποδιδούσης τὰς ἰδέας","chosen":"that assigns the forms to fears in the cheek and to desire","rationale":"The verified παρίᾳ is provisionally read as a dative singular meaning “cheek,” comparable to παρειά, and construed as a locative or somatic dative associated with φόβοις: “fears in the cheek,” perhaps fears manifested facially. This supplies literal English for the printed word, but the attachment and contextual sense remain highly uncertain."},{"source_quote":"ἢ γὰρ φόβῳ τὸν νοῦν πληγεῖσα","chosen":"For, alternatively, when its mind has been struck by fear","rationale":"“For” represents γάρ and “alternatively” represents the printed disjunctive ἢ without adopting the conjectural replacement ἡ."},{"source_quote":"διὰ ὀνείρων τὰς ἰδέας ἀποκυΐσκει","chosen":"it gives birth to the forms through dreams","rationale":"ἀποκυΐσκω uses the image of conceiving or giving birth, here applied to the soul’s production of dream forms."},{"source_quote":"εἰ δὲ ἔσται, οὕτω τὸ τοιοῦτο θεός ἐστιν","chosen":"If, however, it should happen, such a thing is in that way a god","rationale":"The selected text and punctuation present this as a statement. The surrounding reductio could support hearing it rhetorically, but a question is not imposed on the main text."},{"source_quote":"δακτύλῳ δαίμονος","chosen":"by the finger of a demon","rationale":"The rendering retains the concrete image of a demon’s finger as the means by which the apparent change could be produced."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὥστε οὐκέτι ὄναρ ἐπιφανείη ἐκεῖνό ἐστιν","issue":"The relation of optative ἐπιφανείη, neuter ἐκεῖνο, and ἐστιν is syntactically irregular and permits more than one division. The main rendering treats ἐκεῖνο as what might appear and ὄναρ as the predicate, while an alternative understands the phrase more generally as denying that the appearance is merely a dream apparition.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τοῖς παρίᾳ φόβοις καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἀποδιδούσης τὰς ἰδέας","issue":"The image-verified print παρίᾳ can provisionally be identified as a dative singular meaning “cheek,” comparable to παρειά. The main text therefore construes it literally as a locative or somatic dative inserted within τοῖς ... φόβοις, yielding “fears in the cheek.” Although this accounts for every printed word in English, the construction is marked and does not yield a secure contextual sense beside καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ. Corruption remains plausible, but no supported correction has been established or adopted. Because the phrase’s meaning remains unresolved beyond this strained provisional construal, publication remains blocked.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"ἢ γὰρ φόβῳ τὸν νοῦν πληγεῖσα","issue":"The printed ἢ is retained in the main text as a disjunctive represented by “alternatively,” with γάρ represented by “For.” The conjecture ἡ would instead make the feminine article directly introduce πληγεῖσα and yield, “For the soul, when struck in its mind by fear,” but that conjecture is not adopted as the supplied reading.","proposed_reading":"ἡ γὰρ φόβῳ τὸν νοῦν πληγεῖσα","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
